newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Western world nickel mine output up in March - INSG.
newsitem.headline: Western world nickel mine output up in March - INSG.

text.p: Western world nickel mine production rose 1,100 tonnes in March, reaching 61,300 tonnes, the highest monthly total since last June, the International Nickel Study Group (INSG) said in its latest bulletin.

Mine output was strong in all the major origins and the world's leading miner Canada upped its production to 18,100 tonnes from 17,100 in February. Australia and New Caledonia were unchanged at 9,500 and 11,000 tonnes respectively.
Production of primary nickel in the West totalled 58,200 tonnes in March, up from 56,200 a month earlier and again Canada put in a strong figure at 11,800 tonnes up from 11,200.
Japanese output was steady at 10,800 tonnes but New Caledonia's increased to 3,200 from 2,700 tonnes in February. EU output rose by a meagre 200 tonnes to 9,700 tonnes.
On the consumption side, the western world total was little changed at 75,300 tonnes, 400 tonnes down on the previous month.

The fall reflected a slight dip in offtake in the United States -- down 300 tonnes to 13,500. There were also light drops elsewhere in the Americas but these were partly compensated by a rise in EU consumption to 28,100 tonnes from 27,500. The UK's was up 300 tonnes to 3,700.
